The Tarrasch variation of the French Defense is a chess opening that starts with the move 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nd2. Here is a basic guide to playing this variation from the white perspective:

1. e4 e6
2. d4 d5
3. Nd2

The Tarrasch variation aims to control the center with the moves 2.d4 and 3.Nd2, and gain space and time for the development of the pieces. The move 3.Nd2 also prepares to castle kingside and put the king in a more active and secure position.

4. Nc4

This move develops the knight and puts pressure on the d5 pawn. Black can respond with 4...Nf6, which develops the knight and prepares to castle kingside.

5. Bb5

This move develops the bishop and puts pressure on the d5 pawn. It also prepares to castle kingside. Black can respond with 5...a6, which prepares to play ...b5, challenging the bishop and putting pressure on the c4 knight.

6. O-O

This move castles kingside and brings the king to a more active and secure position.

7. a4

This move aims to gain more space and prepares to play ...b5, challenging the bishop.

8. b5

This move challenges the bishop and puts pressure on the d5 pawn.

9. Bxf6

This move captures the bishop and gains material. After 9...exf6, Black will be a pawn down but will have a lead in development.

10. Ne5

This move develops the knight and puts pressure on the d7 pawn.

11. Nxf7

This move sacrifices the knight for two pawns and gains material. After 11...Kxf7, White will be up a pawn and have a lead in development.

12. Qh5

This move puts pressure on the g7 pawn and aims to create a threat of a checkmate.
